name: China's Crewed Lunar Program
short_status: In development: first crewed landing targeted before 2030 (restated by CMSA May 23, 2026); CZ-10A/Mengzhou-1 orbital debut listed by CMSA among its 2026 flights (Nov 2025), though CMSA's Feb 27, 2026 annual plan does not name it and no date has been given; trackers report a slip to 2027 and CMSA has announced no change (as of Nov 2, 2026); CZ-10B variant flew and was recovered Jul 10, 2026; an uncrewed Lanyue lander flight is planned before the crewed landing (CMSA, Oct 22, 2026), and on Oct 31, 2026 CCTV, reporting from CMSA's academic conference, said uncrewed Mengzhou and Lanyue flights are both planned ahead of the crewed landing; no dates given.
tagline: CMSA · China · Programme · 2023 · Commercial and multipolar In development

facts.label: Lunar-landing phase formally announced
facts.value: 29 May 2023, by CMSA deputy director Lin Xiqiang: first Chinese crewed lunar landing before 2030

facts.label: Mission architecture
facts.value: Dual launch: two Long March 10 rockets send the Lanyue lander and the crewed Mengzhou spacecraft separately to lunar orbit for rendezvous and docking. Mengzhou can carry three astronauts between Earth and lunar orbit, and two of them ride Lanyue down to the surface and back (CCTV, 31 Oct 2026, describing the published plan)

facts.label: Surface plan
facts.value: Two astronauts ride the Lanyue lander down for what CMSA calls a short-term stay on the surface (月面短期驻留), with the Tansuo rover. CMSA's program description gives no duration; the widely quoted six hours matches the minimum surface stay CMSA asked for in a 2018 ideas contest for a crewed lander

facts.label: Long March 10 (tri-core lunar version)
facts.value: 92.5 m tall, about 2,189 t at liftoff, 27 t to trans-lunar injection, 70 t to LEO

facts.label: Element names
facts.value: Mengzhou spacecraft and Lanyue lander named 24 Feb 2024; Wangyu lunar suit and Tansuo rover named 12 Feb 2025 (public contests)

facts.label: Mengzhou zero-altitude pad abort
facts.value: 17 Jun 2025, Jiuquan; capsule landed on airbags about 2 minutes after ignition; China's first pad abort test since 1998; declared fully successful

facts.label: Lanyue landing and takeoff test
facts.value: 6 Aug 2025, Huailai, Hebei; full-scale lander flew in a purpose-built extraterrestrial-gravity simulator; first Chinese off-Earth landing-and-ascent trial for a crew vehicle

facts.label: CZ-10 first static fire
facts.value: 15 Aug 2025, LC-301 Wenchang; seven YF-100K engines, thrust near 1,000 t, largest such test ever in China

facts.label: CZ-10 second static fire
facts.value: 12 Sep 2025; seven engines, 320 seconds, including restarts simulating launch, re-entry, and landing for a reusable first stage

facts.label: Prototype stage complete
facts.value: 30 Oct 2025: CMSA spokesperson Zhang Jingbo said CZ-10, Mengzhou, Lanyue, Wangyu suit, and rover "have completed the main work of the prototype stage"

facts.label: In-flight max-Q abort test
facts.value: 11 Feb 2026, LC-301 Wenchang; Mengzhou pulled away about one minute into flight at roughly 10-11 km, at maximum dynamic pressure (Global Times, citing CASC experts, gives about one minute and around 10 km with parachutes near 8 km); capsule recovered from the sea, which CMSA called China's first sea-based search and recovery for a crewed spacecraft; the booster flew a recovery-simulation profile with reentry burn, powered descent and propulsive splashdown at a preset simulated landing point about 200 m from its recovery vessel, according to Zhu Pingping of CASC's China Academy of Launch Vehicle Technology (Science and Technology Daily, 12 Feb 2026)

facts.label: CZ-10B maiden flight and booster recovery
facts.value: 10 Jul 2026, 04:15 UTC, Hainan Commercial Space Launch Site; single-stick cargo variant (16 t to LEO reusable) reached orbit and its first stage was caught by the net system of the Linghang Zhe recovery ship: China's first orbital-booster recovery and the world's first net recovery

facts.label: CZ-10A / Mengzhou-1 orbital debut
facts.value: Listed for 2026 with no date (CMSA's 2026 mission list, Nov 2025, as adjusted on 26 Nov 2025: Tianzhou-10, Shenzhou-23, Shenzhou-24 and Mengzhou-1); CMSA's 27 Feb 2026 annual plan names two crewed flights and one cargo flight for the year without naming Mengzhou-1; uncrewed Mengzhou on the crew-rated CZ-10A single-stick variant; not listed in CMSA's second-half-2026 outlook and reported by trackers as likely slipping to 2027 (China in Space, 18 Jul 2026; it reported again on 20 Oct 2026 that the CZ-10A and then the CZ-10 are expected to debut in 2027), with no official change announced; had NOT flown as of 2 Nov 2026. On 31 Oct 2026 CCTV, reporting from CMSA's academic conference, listed the Long March 10 technology verification flight and the first flights of Mengzhou and Lanyue among tasks the program will complete as planned, with no dates

facts.label: Uncrewed Lanyue flight (announced Oct 22, 2026)
facts.value: CMSA said that under the preliminary overall plan for the landing phase, an uncrewed flight of the Lanyue lander is planned ahead of the crewed landing (拟于载人登月任务前安排揽月着陆器无人飞行任务). It opened a call within China for powered payloads from government bodies, research institutes, educational institutions, enterprises, public institutions and industry organizations: up to 50 kg in total and generally no more than 100 W per mission, with proposals due by 1 March 2027. CMSA gave no date or landing site for the flight.

facts.label: Uncrewed rehearsal plan (CCTV, Nov 2, 2026)
facts.value: Wang Xiang, deputy chief designer of China's crewed space program and chief designer of the Lunar Exploration Project, said in a CCTV report from CMSA's seventh crewed spaceflight academic conference that two principles guide the planning: whatever must be done in lunar orbit is first verified in low Earth orbit, using the space station where possible, and whatever will be done with crew is first flown uncrewed where possible. The uncrewed Lanyue flight is to verify, as far as possible, the key technologies of the whole crewed sequence: reaching lunar orbit, docking with Mengzhou, landing and staying on the surface, lifting off and docking with Mengzhou again (按照无人的状态，把有人状态的全过程，包括发射到环绕月球轨道，跟梦舟飞船交会对接，落月在月面停留，再起飞，重新与梦舟飞船交会对接，全过程的关键技术都要尽可能地验证一遍). No date was given.

facts.label: 2026 program plan
facts.value: 27 Feb 2026 CMSA plan: build out lunar-mission facilities at Wenchang plus tracking, communications, and landing-site ground systems; development "progressing smoothly" toward the before-2030 goal

timeline: CMSA announces the lunar-landing phase: crewed landing before 2030
Spacecraft named Mengzhou ("dream vessel"), lander named Lanyue ("embracing the Moon")
Lunar suit named Wangyu, crew rover named Tansuo, from 9,000+ public entries
Mengzhou zero-altitude pad abort at Jiuquan, first such Chinese test in 27 years; fully successful
Lanyue full-scale landing-and-takeoff test at Huailai, Hebei, in an extraterrestrial-gravity simulator
First CZ-10 static fire at Wenchang LC-301: seven YF-100K engines, ~1,000 t thrust
Second CZ-10 static fire: 320 s with engine restarts for reusability
CMSA: all five major flight products completed the main work of the prototype stage

Max-Q in-flight abort at Wenchang: Mengzhou escapes about one minute into flight at roughly 10-11 km; China's first sea-based recovery of a crewed-spacecraft capsule; booster demonstrates recovery maneuvers
CMSA merges the crewed lunar landing and robotic Chang'e programs across missions, resources and teams into a single 'Lunar Exploration Project' (月球探测工程), and restates the before-2030 landing target
CZ-10B maiden orbital flight; first stage caught in the Linghang Zhe ship's net: China's first orbital-booster recovery
CMSA says an uncrewed Lanyue lander flight is planned before the crewed landing and opens a call for payloads of up to 50 kg, due by 1 Mar 2027; no flight date given
At CMSA's seventh crewed spaceflight academic conference, CCTV reports that uncrewed flights of Mengzhou and Lanyue are planned before the crewed landing; no dates given
